newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian stocks up on back of Lek, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian stocks up on back of Lek, seen rising.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose on Thursday, boosted by a big jump in drug maker Lek.
Market participants said gains could extend into the coming week, with optimism after the central bank's decision to relax foreign investment rules unlikely to fade quickly.
The SBI index rose 1.06 percent or 15.31 points to 1,459.7, taking its rally this week to 15.4 percent.
"I think we can forecast, without exaggerating, that the index could rise to between 1,800 and 1,900 points," said Predrag Stamenkovic, a trader at brokerage BPH.
But some dealers cautioned profit taking could soon set in.
And failure by parliament to make real progress towards ratifying Slovenia's association agreement with the EU by July 15 could send prices into a tailspin, they added.
"Political stability is very important to capital markets. It could result in lower international interest in Slovenian shares for a certain period of time," one dealer said.
The Constitutional Court has ordered parliament to amend the constitution to enable foreigners to buy land before it ratifies the association accord.
Overall four shares rose, 15 fell and nine were untraded. Turnover more than doubled to 874.2 million tolars from 395.3 million.
Traders said petrol trader Petrol, pharmaceutical companies Lek,, Krka and food makers Kolinska and Droga were the most attractive shares for foreign buyers.
Issue C of drug company Lek was the top gainer, jumping 10.0 percent to 30,250 tolars on volume of 27 shares.
Lek's issue A, which is listed in the SBI index, jumped 9.92 percent to 31,900 tolars on volume of 11,224.
Traders said Lek was responding to Wednesday's 18.9 percent rise in its biggest rival Krka, which is listed on the OTC section of Ljubljana bourse.
Krka corrected downwards, falling 4.3 percent or 1,010 tolars to 22,500 tolars on volume of 23,093 shares.
Food company Kolinska was the most active, easing 1.74 percent to 2,200 tolars on volume of 49,042 shares.
Ordinary shares of trading company Kovinotehna led decliners, tumbling 10.32 percent to 426 tolars on volume on volume of 1,772 shares.
Kovinotehna was down in a technical reaction to recent strong gains, traders said.
Petrol rose 2.04 percent to 21,000 tolars on volume of 11,526 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
